## Reading sigma notation {#ss2-reading-sigma .reading-sigma}

<div class="sigma-definition"><span data-math="\sum_{\textcolor{#3b66a8}{k=2}}^{\textcolor{#3b66a8}{4}}\textcolor{#b55224}{(2k+1)}">Sum from k = 2 to 4 of (2k + 1)</span><div><p class="sigma-index-key">Use every integer index from 2 to 4.</p><p class="sigma-rule-key">Substitute each index into the expression.</p><p>Add the resulting values.</p></div></div>

::: {.sigma-substitutions}
::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

$$k=2:\quad 2(2)+1=5$$
:::
::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

$$k=3:\quad 2(3)+1=7$$
:::
::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="2"}

$$k=4:\quad 2(4)+1=9$$
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="3"}
$$\sum_{k=2}^{4}(2k+1)=5+7+9=21$$
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 6 · Summation notation</p>

::: notes
Read aloud: the sum, from k equals 2 to 4, of 2k plus 1. Blue identifies the limits and index; orange identifies the expression. Reveal each substitution separately with Next, then the complete sum. Both endpoints are included. The index is a counter: replacing k consistently by another index letter does not change the sum. Do not use the upper limit as the number of terms unless the lower limit is 1.
:::
